result.keyword: What's the best project management tool for a startup?
result.markdown:
For most startups, I'd recommend **Linear** if you're building a tech or SaaS product, and **ClickUp** if you need one tool to manage the entire business.

The best choice depends on your startup's stage, team size, and whether you're managing product development, marketing, operations, or everything together.

Here's how I'd compare the leading options.

## Best project management tools for startups

![Projects – Linear Docs](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/H7btCzSbelKXdMr_2WS3GWddG9qajBq9JZDHM8HYyOoLV6E4HDh5vlzogddffE6t5gTnGdoZ53UsXuMyPZWPmHRUwQ3ddApfS44CKAri923rLMIeylRQs9HZxmyB23G0rTfX3tmbKwJPdUtZW_x9bJsI8X8b5_Xrbg_k3vvdE22XkcL7igbp9gCGi9QLirCv?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent for product roadmaps, sprints and bug tracking.
- Clean, fast interface.
- Great developer workflows and GitHub integration.
- Less suited to managing an entire non-technical business.

Pricing: Free plan; paid plans available.

[Visit Linear](https://linear.app/)

---

![ClickUp App Reviews and Pricing](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/--zas9FjxB-Om5LISoIR_zv_n_Q2q1AGSTXnIoPKR4vWUYDuZl56oBDv65rnL-X0KLOlsALL5GjKJ03UxWavy3wW86nuOhcD0ZUIj4wKz85sA1zvJmgBv6hQ3cJGAgZixML07EGBK-C0Gf0yKkj39StargdwUd9gZuhawZQI96ng-cS5ILMTVu0C6MejkzkJ?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-rounder)

- Tasks, projects, documents and goals.
- Dashboards and automation.
- Works across marketing, sales, operations and product.
- Can become overwhelming if over-configured.

Pricing: Free plan; paid plans available.

[Visit ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)

---

![Getting started with projects and tasks](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/rBzz0YucWqa7TzwsR7O0OijwcWtKRR6vUa-4dyys2qUThLtS4XfkdJkNbKUF7MlYIx2Pf95vz1ZwpmkGZkQkQJbR9XXSMKgQ3ynqVH_YRdhbdeiYO_anFWUt5rh2LV_lCuu0TZ7Njj7N3y1Z8_one9wjd1Cn5GmMKHW8zKADzpdtXUtH6f9EQMV9lVkrxAxK?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

(Best for early-stage startups)

- Combines project tracking and company documentation.
- Great for SOPs, meeting notes, product specs and company wikis.
- Flexible and easy to customise.
- Less structured for complex project execution.

Pricing: Free plan; paid plans available.

[Visit Notion](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![Introducing Dashboards - a new way to see real-time project data in charts! - Product Launches - Asana Forum](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/wCWLFp4dMEl_v-oRmbowsFC6S4_evWBQMtRxSSXp7OXP6wtqD-ndySpIhbE0vKytZ9TUoZukBYXzktu332gBeqtOvFB5r_4mn9l1GOAEawsVNLrfaNRXIZhTP4IIa9xyWd0YUcL0lL-4dUI7q2c9LjUAelrs03KqyhIOzNbo8gDFWwNUhH6KJIHf5z_4WbFK?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

- Excellent for cross-functional teams.
- Clear task ownership and deadlines.
- Strong project timelines and dependencies.
- Good as teams grow and processes become more structured.

Pricing: Free plan; paid plans available.

[Visit Asana](https://asana.com/)

---

![What's New - monday.com Product Updates](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/A6uqDbwZDZtLi6fdSQ4vBgCQbnekV0PIx4KVuVyvOr829LpE2bCzHdwMLqPfPl8gWESkzkwLYt7S32LGreo4ooKI7LMbOa3LDgEJY5XamBVn4I4fKACcjxheDQNjN3kYBWjEyVTME7rTaH0lrtDPHD2D7YT1KNXf7LC0zf16zSR-GU4N3mIXikR458xkW8a1?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

- Excellent visual project management.
- Good for marketing, sales and operations.
- Custom dashboards and automations.
- Particularly useful for growing teams.

Pricing: Paid plans; check current free/trial options.

[Visit Monday.com](https://monday.com/)

These choices are consistent with recent 2026 startup software comparisons. ## My recommendation by startup type

| Startup situation | My pick |
|--------|--------|
| SaaS / tech startup | Linear |
| General startup, all departments | ClickUp |
| Very early-stage / bootstrapped | Notion |
| Marketing / services business | Asana |
| Scaling team with multiple departments | Monday.com |


## What I'd actually implement

For an early-stage startup, I'd avoid buying too many tools.

A simple setup could be\:

- **Project management\:** ClickUp
- **Company knowledge and documentation\:** Notion
- **Team communication\:** Slack
- **Product development (if applicable)\:** Linear
- **File storage\:** Google Drive

You don't necessarily need all five. Start with one central system and expand only when there's a genuine need.

## A question that would help me narrow it down

What type of startup are you building?
